justification: Real numbers from node tools/verify-page.mjs --drafts /operating-systems/concurrency-race-conditions-locks/, run serially on an otherwise idle machine (CPU ~7-8% before starting, no Chrome/Lighthouse process already running, one run, no re-run needed): words=2921, codeBlocks=26, figures=2, lighthouse performance=97, accessibility=100, best-practices=100, seo=100; consoleErrors=0; consoleWarnings=0; broken links=0; mobileOverflowPx=0; screenshotParts desktop-light=11, desktop-dark=11, mobile-light=16, mobile-dark=16. The only verify-page failure is the expected placeholder text: NEEDS_MARKUS (byline/bio/legal-name markers), matching the accepted exception in docs/WRITER_GUIDE.md. I read every desktop-light part (01-11) and every mobile-dark part (01-16) in full, plus spot-checked desktop-dark (fold, 02, 03, 05, 06) and mobile-light (fold, 03, 08) at the fold and at both figures. Both hand-written SVG diagrams -- Figure 1 (the four-step read/read/write/write interleaving that loses an update) and Figure 2 (the two-node wait-for cycle: thread A holds lock A and wants lock B, thread B holds lock B and wants lock A) -- use <figure class="diagram">, role="img" with unique-prefixed <title>/<desc> ids, and theme classes (d-box-2/d-box-bad/d-box-accent, d-accent/d-bad strokes, d-text-bad, d-muted, d-small/d-mono/d-bold) rather than literal colors; both are 360-wide viewBoxes that render at native width with no sideways scroll or faded edge at 390px, and stayed fully legible (box borders, arrow colors, and small labels all readable) in all four theme/width combinations checked, including the red 'counter is still 1: A's write is gone' / bad-colored write box in Figure 1 and the dashed red wait arrows with 'wants lock A' / 'wants lock B' labels in Figure 2. All four exercises (fake lock, three-way deadlock, semaphore cost, fix-the-transfer) stayed correctly collapsed behind <details>/'Show solution' in every screenshot checked -- no solution code or output leaked before the toggle, including the exercises whose solution is itself a full runnable program with its own output panel. Heading hierarchy is clean (single H1, ## for the eight major sections, no skipped levels, only ##/### in 'On this page'), and the prose/code/diagram/exercise rhythm never runs long without a break: the longest stretch of unbroken prose is about one paragraph before the next code block, diagram, or exercise. The one callout (:::pitfall, 'Interlocked only reaches as far as the one operation you call' / 'ensure that any write or read access to a shared variable is atomic') renders as a clearly distinct red-tinted bordered box with icon in both light and dark screenshots, not just a colored rule. All 'text output' panels that carry the article's actual evidence -- expected: 8,000,000 / actual: [...] / lost: [...] / counter == expected: False, the True/False booleans after each fix, lock: [...] ms / Interlocked: [...] ms, peak concurrent users: 2, hits["page-views"] == expected: True, and the timed-out/stalled booleans -- fit inside the ~40-column mobile window with nothing operative cut off; the specific numbers called out in the prompt (8,000,000, the 2_000_000-per-thread constant, the ms timings) were checked directly and the output-panel instances of all of them are fully visible. Compared against the two most relevant real pages: Microsoft's own 'The lock statement' reference (one of this article's own cited sources, fetched directly) is plain prose and one code sample with no diagram of any kind, no visualization of the interleaving or deadlock it describes, and no verification that the sample's claimed output ('Account's balance is 2000') is actually machine-checked; a representative GeeksforGeeks deadlock page (fetched directly) has only static, non-theme-aware clip-art-style diagrams (a resource-cycle image with no confirmed dark-mode variant) and no runnable or verified code at all. This article's two original, theme-correct SVGs that visually re-enact the exact bug in prose (the interleaving that loses an update, the wait-for cycle that deadlocks), its 26 machine-verified C#/.NET code blocks with real measured numbers from a stated test machine, and its four exercises with checkable, collapsed solutions put it clearly ahead of both on design/illustration depth for this topic, not merely at parity. Net: this is a very clean, close-to-flawless design pass with no rendering defects found in either theme at either width; the deductions below are both minor and neither blocks the article.

issues.location: The three matched counter-demo code blocks (lost-update, with-lock, with-interlocked) and their 'Cost' variant -- the `const int IncrementsPerThread = 2_000_000;` declaration line and its `for (int j = 0; j < IncrementsPerThread; j++)` usage line
issues.problem: Both lines run past the ~40-column visible window on mobile (390px) in every screenshot they appear in (e.g. mobile-dark-part01, mobile-dark-part05, mobile-light-part03), so the trailing digits of `2_000_000` and the `Thread; j++)` tail of the for-loop line sit under the fade. The value itself is boilerplate repeated four times verbatim, and the prose immediately above and below each block states 'two million increments per thread' / '8,000,000' in full, so nothing the reader needs is actually lost -- this is the 'tail is boilerplate, not the point' case the writer guide treats as fine, but it is a recurring pattern worth a look if the writer wants tighter mobile framing.
issues.fixLooksLike: Optional: shorten to `const int IncrementsPerThread = 2_000_000;` -> a shorter identifier, or break the for-loop condition after `j <` onto its own indent, so the operative numeral sits fully inside the first 40 columns on mobile. Not required for the pass gate since the output panels that carry the real evidence are unaffected.

issues.location: site-wide performance profile (affects this route's Lighthouse run; not this article's markup)
issues.problem: Lighthouse performance is 97 (comfortably clears the round's >=90 gate) but does not saturate: sub-audits First Contentful Paint (0.87, 1.9s), Max Potential FID (0.56, 230ms), 'Reduce unused CSS' (0.5, 14 KiB), Document request latency (0.5, 141 KiB est. savings), and 'Page prevented back/forward cache restoration' (0, 2 failure reasons) all show room. These match the same shared-shell pattern noted in other articles' design reviews (e.g. testing/test-doubles round 1), so this looks like page-shell/script behavior common to every route rather than anything specific to this article's content.
issues.fixLooksLike: Integrator investigates the bf-cache blocker (commonly an unload/beforeunload listener or a no-store cache header) and the unused-CSS/document-latency savings across the shared layout; likely a global fix that lifts every article's score rather than a per-article change.
